title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck
description: The potential $\Psi = \frac{k}{2}(x^2 + y^2)$ with $k = 1$ pulls every particle back to the origin with force $-kX$, so $dX_t = -kX_t\,dt + \sigma\,dW_t$. All particles start at $(3, 2)$. Press play and watch the Observable window ($\mathbb{E}|X_t|^2$ against the exact value under the stationary law).

questions.text: Does the cloud keep spreading as in Brownian motion? Describe what happens to its centre and its size.
Stationary value of $\mathbb{E}|X_t|^2$ for σ = 0.8, k = 1?
Give the stationary variance of one coordinate as a formula in σ and k.
Set σ = 1.2. New stationary value of $\mathbb{E}|X_t|^2$?
How long does it take to get there? Compare with the relaxation rate $k$ of the mean, $\mathbb{E}X_t = e^{-kt}X_0$.
